objectives: Calculate a plant's capacity factor and full-load hours from its yearly output
Explain why capacity factor is not an efficiency and why cost per kilowatt alone misleads
Use the levelized cost of energy (LCOE) equation to predict how capacity factor and interest rates change the cost

questions.prompt: A 50 MW wind farm delivers 153,300 MWh in a year. What is its capacity factor?
questions.explain: CF = 153,300 ÷ (50 × 8,760) = 0.35. 3,066 hours is the farm's full-load hours (0.35 × 8,760): the same information said another way, not the capacity factor itself.

questions.prompt: The US coal fleet ran at a capacity factor of 42.6 % in 2024. What does that tell you?
choices: Coal plants turned 42.6 % of their fuel's energy into electricity
Coal made 42.6 % of all US electricity that year
The fleet made 42.6 % of what it could at full output all year, partly because it was asked to run less
Coal plants were broken down for 57.4 % of the year
questions.explain: Capacity factor compares the year's energy with running flat out for all 8,760 hours; it is not an efficiency or a share of the country's electricity. For coal and gas it also reflects how often the plants were asked to run, not only how often they could.

questions.prompt: In the worked example, utility solar costs 40.4 $/MWh at a capacity factor of 0.17. Keeping every other input the same, what is the LCOE at a sunnier site with a capacity factor of 0.25?
choices: About 40 $/MWh, since the build cost is unchanged
questions.explain: With no fuel or variable costs, solar's LCOE is its yearly cost divided by the energy it makes, so it scales as 1/CF: 40.4 × 0.17 ÷ 0.25 ≈ 27 $/MWh. 59 $/MWh multiplies by the ratio instead of dividing; the same yearly payment spread over more megawatt-hours makes each one cheaper.

questions.prompt: Why does utility solar's LCOE depend so strongly on the discount rate?
choices: A higher discount rate lowers the capacity factor of the farm
A higher discount rate makes the panels wear out sooner
Solar's fuel price is tied to the interest rate
About four-fifths of its cost is repaying the up-front build cost with interest
questions.explain: In the worked example the loan repayment is 32.0 of the 40.4 $/MWh, about four-fifths of the total: solar is almost all capital, so the interest rate on that capital drives its cost. Solar has no fuel cost at all, and the discount rate does not change how much sunshine the farm gets.
